chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Yazid al-Kunasi, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
"When the girl reaches nine years, orphanhood departs from her, she may be married, and the full legal penalties are established upon her and for her."

He said: I said, "If a boy is married by his father and consummates with his wife while he has not yet attained maturity, are the legal penalties carried out upon him while he is in that state?" He said: So he said, "As for the complete legal penalties by which adult men are taken, no. But he is flogged in all the legal penalties according to the extent of his age, and that is applied to him for what is between him and fifteen years of age. And the limits of Allah are not nullified among His creation, nor are the rights of the Muslims among themselves nullified."

key_terms.حُقُوقُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ: the rights owed between Muslims in legal and social dealings
key_terms.خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً: fifteen years of age; the upper age limit mentioned for this stage
key_terms.غَيْرُ مُدْرِكٍ: not yet mature; not having fully attained legal discernment or adulthood
key_terms.ٱلْجَارِيَةُ: a young girl; here, a female reaching the age of legal responsibility
key_terms.ٱلْحُدُودُ: prescribed legal penalties set by Allah
key_terms.ٱلْحُدُودُ ٱلْكَامِلَةُ: the complete legal penalties applied to fully legally accountable adult men
key_terms.ٱلْيُتْمُ: orphanhood; the legal state of being treated as an orphan

ai.seo_question: When do legal penalties and marital rulings begin to apply to boys and girls in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal responsibility in relation to age, distinguishing between the rulings for a girl who reaches nine years and a boy who has not yet fully attained maturity. It explains that full hudud apply differently based on legal age, while still affirming that the limits of Allah and the rights of Muslims are not to be neglected.
